title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

reports.title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

summary:
On Aug. 3 in a Cypress neighborhood, Harris County sheriff's deputies surrounded a Camaro driven by Anthony, 19, as he was leaving after a gas station run with his friend Julian, also 19. At least five patrol cars and a helicopter responded after deputies thought the car was stolen, based on a license plate alert for a similar Camaro linked to several aggravated robberies. Deputies pointed guns, handcuffed both men, and forced Julian to the ground, causing cuts and scrapes. Julian said a deputy threatened to shoot and kill him. Only after the handcuffing did deputies check and realize they had the wrong car.

Anthony's mother, Leslie, said the deputies had time to run the plates or make a normal traffic stop, and she plans to hire an attorney. The sheriff's office said supervisors will review body camera footage to see if procedures were followed. Both men were told how to file a formal complaint with internal affairs, and they plan to do so.
title_en: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say
